findings.evidence:
green-check.test.sh:867-870 compares with `$5 == n`. Both operands are numeric strings, so awk compares them NUMERICALLY. Reproduced directly: `printf '6.123
6.1230
6.12300
' | awk -v n='6.1230' '{print ($1==n), (("x" $1)==("x" n))}'` reports all three numerically EQUAL while prefixed textual comparison distinguishes them. 13.A-META-3 at :983-996 builds its bystander with GC13_NONCE+1, which can never produce a trailing-zero alias.
findings.description: CARRIED FROM R6-F3, STATUS PARTIAL. The round-7 fix introduced a per-run PID nonce to establish ownership, and the nonce itself is sound -- PID reuse cannot occur while the owning script is alive, the fractional duration survives `ps -axo args=`, and the retained PGID layer is harmless narrowing. But the COMPARISON defeats it: distinct PID tokens whose decimal spellings differ only by trailing zeroes alias. Two concurrent same-PGID invocations with PIDs 123 and 1230 produce `sleep 6.123` and `sleep 6.1230`; either cleanup selects both and can SIGKILL the other invocation's target -- precisely the case the nonce was introduced to close. The control cannot see it because of how the bystander token was chosen. FIX: force textual comparison, e.g. `("x" $5) == ("x" n)`, verified on both BWK awk (macOS) and mawk (Ubuntu 24.04's default), and add a same-PGID control whose token is a numeric alias such as ${GC13_NONCE}0.

findings.evidence: `make verify-release 'RELEASE_TAG=v$(id)'` emitted `verify-release-manifest.sh: manifests/v.sha256 has not been frozen yet` -- make expanded `$(id)` to empty before the shell saw anything. Existing Section 5 legs use semicolon-bearing values and never test literal dollar-parenthesis preservation.
findings.description: The recipe comment claims RELEASE_TAG is forwarded as exactly one untouched word and that make itself never touches the value, citing legal `v$(id)`. GNU make recursively expands command-line variables when exporting them into the recipe environment, so make consumes the expression first. The SHELL-injection fix from R6-F2 is sound and unaffected -- nothing executes -- but the documented local override cannot actually verify that legal tag, and the comment asserts otherwise. FIX: normalise the raw command-line value into a simply-expanded exported variable without evaluating it and add a round-trip leg for `v$(id)`, or document plainly that make consumes `$(...)`/`${...}` in RELEASE_TAG.

findings.evidence: cmd_classify() at workflow-manifest.sh:924-938 falls through to replace-custom when source bytes differ and no oldhash exists. Section 4d tests only the absent, stock-HOOKS, edited-HOOKS and current-target shapes -- never a pre-existing or edited CODEX_SETUP.md.
findings.description: Claims that because CODEX_SETUP.md is absent from the old table it can ONLY ever classify as copy-new or skip-current. False: an operator who already has docs/CODEX_SETUP.md, or who edits it after installation, produces differing source bytes with no oldhash, and cmd_classify selects replace-custom. The case is neither acknowledged nor tested. FIX: remove the universal, or add and describe the edited/pre-existing case.

findings.evidence: Section 5 checks only that v4 marker rows are absent; it never classifies against a wrong-tree table. workflow-manifest.sh:919-938 shows the unchanged outcomes for the customized and missing-target cases.
findings.description: Claims that generating the old table from the wrong tree would make EVERY customization verdict wrong in the safest-looking direction. False, and with no negative control: a genuinely customized workflow or operator target still yields replace-custom/preserve-custom even when the erroneous old hash equals the current source hash, and a missing target still yields copy-new. FIX: delete the characterisation per the waiver ruling, or replace it with a narrowly tested scenario.

findings.evidence: Lines 1180-1192 inspect only the rubric preserve-custom result and the backend replace-stock result.
findings.description: Claims that after removing the operator-verdict block the other five verdicts are unaffected, while the mutant path actually checks only replace-stock. Merge, copy-new, skip-current and replace-custom are never checked against the mutant, so a future mutation touching one of those branches leaves the test green while the comment still claims five-verdict coverage. FIX: assert all five unaffected rows, or narrow the prose to the one control actually checked.

findings.evidence: Lines 702-704 state a roughly two-second sweep grace; lines 713-725 describe the surviving argv as bare `sleep 6`; line 818 actually installs `sleep 6.$GC13_NONCE`.
findings.description: Both statements went stale when the nonce landed. A `sleep 6.<pid>` killed around 3.2 seconds in has roughly 2.8-3.8 seconds remaining, not the claimed margin, and its argv carries the nonce-bearing fractional argument. A maintainer could remove the explicit reap trusting the stated sweep margin, or restore a bare-argv selector trusting the stale description, reintroducing either survivor failures or cross-run matching. FIX: state that the margin comes from later sections plus the explicit ownership-filtered cleanup rather than the sweep grace, and describe the actual nonce-bearing argv.
